The preliminary Travel Panel survey results for 2024 suggest that daily auto trips (personal vehicles) have decreased since 2021 from a 56% mode share to a 45.6% mode share. 

• Walk mode share remained stable at 29% compared to 2023 but up from 26% in 2021. • Cycling mode share remains at 7% (including micromobility) • Transit mode share increased to 17%, although still below the 18% survey result in 2019, before the pandemic. A number of factors may contribute to the trends observed above: • the impact of the pandemic on human activity patterns; • increased work-from-home and hybrid work schedules. • The overall daily trip rate increased slightly from 2.9 trips per person in 2022 to 3.2 trips per person in 2024, accounting for an additional 144,000 daily trips in 2024 compared to 2023. This is down from an average of 3.7 trips per person in 2019 before telecommuting became popular during the onset of the COVID-19 global pandemic.

Belfast have also committed to producing a Low Emissions Vehicle Strategy that will align with a regional version being produced for Northern Ireland.

The figures do not sum to 100% since this is just for commuting and the American Community Survey includes telecommute and/or telework as a \'trip\' type. Finally, the 'other' means of commuting as listed under ACS is assumed to be biking or other micro mobility, as biking and e-scooter commute trips have accelerated in recent years from expansion of DC's bike share program, increased scooter popularity, and increased bike trail and protected lane network miles. These are lumped together under \'cycling\' in this table. \n\nThe District has historical (2011) and projected (2040) freight flow data by weight and value, demonstrating that trucking is the mode by which the overwhelming majority of freight inbound, within, outbound, and through the District travels, with a small fraction of through-traffic freight traveling via rail and a small fraction on in-bound freight coming via water.

Collective transport 30% / 66% / 77%

column37: Passenger mode share values were calculated based on VMT data from the most recent Google Environmental Insights Explorer data (for 2023.) 100% of in-boundary trips and 50% of inbound and outbound trips were included in calculations. The number given for “private motorized transport” includes motorcycles and all automobiles, including taxis and shared vehicles. Cells left blank are unknown. Rail travel was too small a percent of overall travel to be included in the Google dataset. Freight mode share values were calculated based on VMT data from the California Air Resource Board's EMFAC model (https://arb.ca.gov/emfac/emissions-inventory) for Santa Clara County for 2023. The model does not distinguish between freight and passenger traffic, only between different vehicle types - so while some vehicle types were excluded from this analysis that definitely are not used for freight (eg school buses), vehicle types used for both passenger and freight traffic were included. For this reason, this breakdown likely overestimates the amount of freight transport by motorcycle and light goods vehicles. Regarding rail freight, freight rail does pass through the city, but San Jose does not have a freight rail depot. We do not have data to calculate mode share of freight rail.

Data dihitung dengan membandingkan jumlah kendaraan pribadi (sepeda motor dan mobil penumpang) dengan jumlah pengguna angkutan umum, khususnya bus.

umlah Kendaraan Bermotor 2023
1. Sepeda Motor :	2.546.422 unit
2. Mobil Penumpang :	482.182 unit
3. Mobil Bus : 9.457 unit
4. Mobil Barang : 157.696 unit
5. Kendaraan Khusus : 174 unit
Total Kendaraan	3.195.931 unit

A. Data Pengguna Angkutan Umum (Bus)
Jumlah Pengguna Transportasi Bus, terdapat 5 koridor.
Jika dirata-ratakan dari data 2023:
Total pengguna bus per bulan: ± 150.000 - 160.000 penumpang.
Total pengguna bus per tahun (2023): ± 1,8 juta - 2 juta penumpang.
Rasio terhadap populasi Kota Medan (±2,5 juta jiwa): Hanya sekitar 6-8% penduduk yang menggunakan bus secara rutin.

B. Pangsa Moda Penumpang
Pangsa dihitung berdasarkan jumlah pengguna angkutan umum dibandingkan kendaraan pribadi.
Mayoritas mobilitas penduduk Kota Medan masih didominasi oleh sepeda motor, sementara pangsa transportasi publik seperti bus masih sangat kecil, jauh dari target 30% pangsa angkutan umum nasional.

C. Pangsa Moda Angkutan Barang
Berdasarkan data kendaraan bermotor:
Mobil barang hanya 4,94% dari total kendaraan di Kota Medan.
Angkutan barang berbasis jalan raya masih dominan karena:
- Aktivitas logistik dari Pelabuhan Belawan.
- Belum optimalnya jalur kereta api barang di wilayah Medan.

1. Moda penumpang di Kota Medan didominasi sepeda motor (79,70%) dan mobil pribadi (15,09%), sementara bus hanya menyumbang <10% dari mobilitas masyarakat.
2. Moda angkutan barang berbasis jalan hanya 4,94% dari total kendaraan, tetapi memiliki dampak signifikan terhadap kemacetan dan emisi.

Based on Sustainable Energy Transition document transport activities in 2019: 56 billion passenger-kilometers with assumed growth of 4% per annum and for freight mode share data taken from Low Carbon Mobility (LCM) 2021, https://www.mgtc.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Low-Carbon-Mobility-Blueprint-2021-2030.pdf . The transport sector energy demand will continue to dominate Iskandar Malaysia's TFEC, and is projected to increase from 2,559 ktoe in 2019 to 3,141 ktoe in 2030. In 2030, the sub-sector share of transport energy demand is projected to be road passenger transport 1,784 ktoe (56.8%) and road freight transport 1,357 ktoe (43.2%). Road passenger transport is subdivided into six subcategories, i.e., private cars, motorbikes, taxis and E-hailing, buses, BRT and others. The rate of public transport use will be increased from 17% in 2019 to 41% (in terms of passenger-km travelled) in 2030, while reducing the use of private passenger cars and motorbikes by 18.5% and 5%, respectively. This allows substantial energy demand reduction due to increased uptake of more efficient transport modes. The passenger transport demand is expected to decrease by 789 ktoe in 2030, compared to the BAU scenario. Registered vehicle statistics for the State of Johor are provided by the Road Transport Department Malaysia. This is further approximated for Iskandar Malaysia population ratio of 0.59 (IM/Johor) and the assumption that 70% of the total registered vehicles are active on the road. Iskandar Malaysia aimed for 50% vehicle mode share between public and private transport by 2050 (page 224, Low Carbon Society Blueprint Climate Action Plan 2030), while aiming for 60% of electric vehicle will be dominating the road. Based on the Low Carbon Mobility Blue-print LCMB Survey, walking is competitive and could be promoted as an effective
first-last mile mode at shorter distances, i.e.<500m. Similarly, the bicycle mode
could also be a competitive first-last mile mode for access distance below 1,500m
from public transit nodes. However, the weather in Malaysia may not permit walking or NMT as the first-last mile because of the weather is hot, humid as well as rainy season, make it inconvenience to promote further. Taking into consideration this challenge, the government has into consideration improving the infrastructure of pedestrian walkaway for example putting the rooftop to promote more NMT and induced healthy lifestyle for the users.

Reparto modal del transporte en Montería

Según el estudio técnico del Sistema Estratégico de Transporte Público de Montería:

El 29,5 % de los viajes diarios en la ciudad se realizan usando transporte público formal (buses y colectivos).

Otros modos incluyen caminar (32,4 %), bicicleta (17,9 %), moto particular o mototaxi (17,5 %) y medios informales o no motorizados menores (2,7 %). 

Medio de transporte	% de viajes diarios
Transporte público (bus/colectivo)	29,5 %
A pie	32,4 %
Bicicleta	17,9 %
Moto (particular o mototaxi)	17,5 %
Otros medios informales	2,7 %

Este reparto modal se basa en datos de diseño conceptual del SETP de Montería, elaborado en 2009, pero constituye una de las pocas estimaciones detalladas disponibles públicamente.

El uso de mototaxi puede considerarse transporte informal, aunque cumple funciones similares al transporte público.
Conclusión

En Montería, aproximadamente el 29,5 % de los viajes diarios se realiza en transporte público formal.

El transporte informal (moto o mototaxi) y modos no motorizados (caminar o bicicleta) capturan una parte significativa del reparto modal.

A Secretaria de Mobilidade de Santo André, no âmbito do desenvolvimento do Observatório da Mobilidade, coletou dados da Pesquisa Origem e Destino 2023 realizada pelo Metrô/SP para embasar análises sobre os padrões de deslocamento no município. Os resultados revelam uma distribuição modal marcada pela predominância do transporte motorizado particular, seguido por modos ativos e coletivos, com nuances importantes a serem consideradas: forte predominância do transporte motorizado particular, que responde por 53,89% do total de viagens. Esse dado reflete a significativa dependência de veículos particulares automóveis e motocicletas, como principal opção de deslocamento da população, possivelmente influenciada por fatores como a extensão territorial, a cultura de mobilidade baseada no automóvel e limitações percebidas na oferta de alternativas coletivas ou não motorizadas.
Em seguida, observa-se que os modos ativos como caminhada (25,66%) e bicicleta (0,41%), juntos representam mais de um quarto das viagens. O expressivo percentual de deslocamentos a pé indica sua relevância para viagens curtas ou em áreas com alta adensamento.
O transporte coletivo formal, representado por ônibus (6,28%) e trem/metrô (3,93%), soma cerca de 10% das viagens, um percentual modesto para uma região metropolitana, indicando desafios de cobertura, confiabilidade ou atratividade desses modos. Por outro lado, os serviços por aplicativo (4,55%) já superam o transporte público em participação, mostrando como novas tecnologias vêm influenciando as preferências de mobilidade.
Os demais modos, incluindo transporte fretado, escolar e a categoria genérica “outros”, têm participação residual. A pesquisa não capturou modos emergentes como patinetes elétricos ou transportes informais, limitando a análise completa do espectro modal. Esses dados reforçam a necessidade de políticas integradas que ampliem e qualifiquem a oferta de transporte público, incentivem modos ativos e regulamentem novas formas de mobilidade.

1.Passenger transportation figures are calculated based on the original questionnaire data from the '2022 Survey of People's Daily Means of Transportation' conducted by the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (central government):
（1）Based on the “Modal Share of Trips Made by Residents of New Taipei City” statistics table, using the proportion of trips made by residents of New Taipei City.
（2）According to the existing data, it is currently not possible to break down the share of informal/feeder transport/mass transit systems in the total passenger transport modes; therefore, the value is entered as 0.
（3）In the statistical tables published by the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, ferries are categorized under “Other Modes of Transport,” and shared cars/motorcycles are categorized under “Private Vehicles.”

2.Freight transportation was calculated based on the '2024 Freight Transportation Survey Report' conducted by the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, as well as the '2024 Volume of Goods Transported at Stations of the Taiwan Railways Administration':
(1)Motorcycles: There is no available data on freight transported by motorcycles. Additionally, it is not possible to distinguish whether motorcycles are used for delivery services. Therefore, this category is reported as zero.
(2)Trucks (small, medium, and large): Data on freight tonnage by trucks in New Taipei City were sourced from the 2024 Motor Vehicle Freight Survey Report. Based on vehicle-kilometer transport demand patterns, the tonnage was divided as follows: small trucks account for 66.7%, while medium and large trucks combined account for 33.3%.
(3)Rail Transport: Rail freight volume in New Taipei City was estimated by taking the total tonnage of goods 'arriving at and dispatched from' stations within the city from the 2024 Taiwan Railways Statistical Yearbook and dividing by two. Since the yearbook only reports freight volumes by railway line rather than by station, the 2020 distribution ratios by station were used to estimate the breakdown for each station.
(4)No Inland Water Transport: There is no inland water transport system within the jurisdiction of New Taipei City.

The jurisdiction of Çanakkale demonstrates a diverse transport modal split for both passenger and freight movement. Passenger transport is primarily dominated by private motorized vehicles, accounting for approximately 60% of trips, followed by bus services at around 28%, and informal transit such as minibuses and shared taxis making up about 18%. Active modes like walking and cycling constitute a smaller yet significant share, with estimated values of 7% and 3% respectively. Emerging micromobility options, including e-scooters, currently represent under 1% of the modal share.

On the freight side, road transport remains the predominant mode, estimated at 70%, due to the flexibility and coverage of the highway network. Maritime transport plays a crucial role given Çanakkale's strategic location and port facilities, accounting for roughly 25% of freight movement. Rail freight comprises a smaller share, around 5%, reflecting limited rail infrastructure in the region.

These modal shares highlight the importance of multi-modal integration and the potential to increase sustainable transport options within the jurisdiction, particularly in expanding public transport and active mobility, as part of the ongoing climate action and urban development plans.

El municipio de Durango enfrenta retos y oportunidades clave en materia ambiental y climática. Por un lado, cuenta con alta cobertura eléctrica (98 %) y disponibilidad prácticamente continua del servicio, lo que asegura condiciones básicas para la vida urbana. Sin embargo, la pobreza energética persiste en ciertos sectores, sobre todo rurales o marginados, donde los hogares aún dependen de combustibles sólidos, lo que impacta la salud y la equidad social.

En movilidad, se observa una fuerte dependencia del vehículo particular (≈38 %), mientras que el uso de transporte público colectivo es bajo (≈12 %) y los viajes en bicicleta (≈9 %) o a pie (60-70 %) tienen un peso considerable, reflejando tanto limitaciones de infraestructura como potencial para avanzar hacia un modelo de movilidad sostenible. El transporte de carga y motocicletas también representan fracciones importantes que deben gestionarse con seguridad y normatividad.

La disponibilidad de recursos financieros, humanos y técnicos condiciona directamente el alcance de las políticas ambientales municipales: con recursos limitados, las acciones se reducen a programas aislados; con mayor financiamiento y coordinación con el gobierno estatal y federal, se pueden ejecutar proyectos integrales de reforestación, eficiencia energética y resiliencia climática.

En suma, la transición hacia un modelo más sostenible en Durango requiere:

Coordinación estrecha entre el municipio y el estado, para alinear metas y asegurar financiamiento.

Priorización de equidad social en las políticas climáticas, garantizando que los beneficios lleguen a los grupos más vulnerables.

Impulso de movilidad sustentable y áreas verdes urbanas, para mitigar el calor extremo y mejorar la calidad de vida.

Fortalecimiento institucional para planear, ejecutar y evaluar con indicadores claros los impactos de la acción climática.

The Council as Local Transport Authority (LTA) is currently working alongside other Lancashire LTAs (Lancashire County Council and Blackpool Borough Council) to prepare a new Local Transport for Lancashire, referred to as LTP4. A Green Paper has been prepared evidencing the big economic, social and environmental challenges facing the county, and how they are all inter-related and affected by transport. Better transport can be an important part of a cross-sector solution. The the 3 LTAs will be undertaking stakeholder engagement over the coming months to identify a new transport vision, objectives, and start discussions around policies and programmes to support those objectives over the next 10+ years. 

It is anticipated that LTP4 will focus on the avoid-shift-improve hierarchy (i.e. substituting trips as a priority where possible, then modal shift to more active travel and sustainable public transport options, and finally switching fuels as rapidly as possible).

Blackburn with Darwen Council are already progressing a number of workstreams at the local level, in advance of LTP4, that works towards the transport hierarchy set out above, and aim of decarbonising the local transport systems:

•	A new Local Plan (adopted January 2024) and Climate Impacts Framework SPD that helps to support development in locations where there is a reduced need to travel
•	An Infrastructure Delivery Plan, including an up-to-date Bus Service Improvement Plan (BSIP), and Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan (LCWIP), to ensure that attractive and accessible infrastructure options are provided locally to encourage modal shift
•	A programme of work around 'hearts and minds' for active travel, including creation of a local brand identity, campaign programme, improved data and evidence collection and public engagement, and walk to school outreach projects (school streets audits, WOW etc.); and 
•	Acceleration of publicly available electric vehicle chargepoint locations for on-street charging, through local charging hubs and cable-tray solutions

Transportation mode share data is taken from Google's Environmental Insights Explorer (EIE) for the year 2023.
Currently, EIE provides distance traveled and number of trips for all travel that begins and/or ends in the city. It does not include trips that begin and end outside the city. The full distance traveled for trips beginning and/or ending inside the boundary is included. The EIE default unit for vehicle distance traveled is kilometers (VKT).
To use EIE data with the GPC induced-activity method, the City has calculated the appropriate induced-activity VKT by counting all of the in-boundary distance traveled and 50% of the inbound and outbound distance to create the mode share numbers reported here.

column37: Accurate mode share data across the full range of journey purposes doesn't exist in Wales at present. The current situation is that some reasonably good data exists for journey to work mode share (as that question is asked quite regularly in surveys). For all other journey purposes assessments are currently based on a wide range of trip volume data sources, which are then combined into trip matrices for use in the multi-modal transport models; mode share estimates are extracted from this. It is believed this data gap situation will change in the next 2 years as a new Wales National Travel Survey is rolled out that is equivalent to the survey that takes place in England, where each year a sample of the population is asked to complete a travel diary, logging all of their journeys and mode choices over a week period. Updated modal share data is expected March 2026. Until that time, their are some limitations in what mode share information we can obtain. However, two data sources that do exist: 1. National Survey for Wales (National Survey for Wales GOV.WALES) Normally the only transport question asked is whether or not respondents have access to a car. However in 2019/20 there was a focus on transport and the question on 'usual mode of travel to work' (which includes 16 education trips as well) was asked. Results were as follows: • Car/Van: 75.0% • Walk/Run: 13.0% • Bus/Minibus/Coach: 5.8% • Train: 3.0% • Cycle: 1.7%

Al analizar el destino de estos viajes, es posible ver que el 97,73% terminan en la misma comuna.En la comuna se originaban 11.834 viajes en el modo bicicleta el año 2001 (SECTRA, 2003) mientras que el 2012 esta cifra sube a 25.384, es decir, hubo un aumento de un 114,5%.Al interior de la comuna se originan 25.384 viajes en bicicleta, lo que es equivalente al 7,55% del total de viajes (SECTRA, 2014). Sin embargo, al contrastar este valor con el porcentaje de infraestructura vial dedicada a la bicicleta (ciclovías) en la comuna, se ve una gran disparidad, donde tan solo 1,10% de la infraestructura vial está dedicada a ciclovías. El transporte público absorbe el 27,3% de los viajes originados en la comuna, solo superado por los desplazamientos realizados a pie (39,07%). Es el medio de transporte más utilizado cuando se trata de viajes hacia otras comunas con un promedio de 63,11 minutos por viaje. Estos traslados se concentran en el sector oriente de Renca, particularmente en el sector del Centro Cívico y alrededor de la Ruta 5.El 16 de noviembre de 2022 el sistema de Red Metropolitana de Movilidad (RED) inauguró el primer terminal de buses que se construye como mitigación de un privado en Renca, con capacidad para estacionar más de 20 buses, en una superficie de terreno de más de 10 mil m2 y 246 m2 construidos.En Renca se originan 7.002 viajes en los modos taxi y colectivo en un día laboral normal del 2012. Esto corresponde al 2,15% de la partición modal. El principal destino de estos viajes es al interior de Renca, pero seguido muy de cerca por la comuna de Santiago, la cual atrae un poco más de un tercio de estos viajes. El modo auto concentra el 17,42% de los viajes originados en Renca en un día laboral normal del 2012, es decir, 56.760 viajes. Este es utilizado por la gente de más ingresos de la comuna. Para este análisis se consideró la información asociada a la partición modal de viajes Originados y Terminados en Renca para un día laboral promedio del año 2012. The mode share in our jurisdiction shows that most trips are made through public and private transport, while walking and cycling continue to play an important role in daily mobility. This highlights the need to strengthen public transport systems and expand active mobility infrastructure to promote more sustainable and climate-resilient urban transport. The City Government of Butuan (CGB), through the City Transportation and Traffic Management Department (CTTMD), is committed to this vision through various initiatives. Among these is the Car-Free Sunday program, which provides a dedicated space for walking, cycling, and community engagement, promoting healthier and low-carbon transport options.

In support of active transport development, we have already conducted an Active Transport Planning Workshop in collaboration with the Department of Transportation (DOTr), as part of the preparatory activities for the formulation of our Active Transportation Plan. In parallel, the city has embarked on a Tricycle Modernization Program, which includes a phased fleet modernization target of 25% per year from 2025 to 2028, aiming to reduce emissions and improve the quality of public transport services.

Moreover, the recently approved Local Public Transport Route Plan (LPTRP) Ordinance and Traffic and Road Use Plan (TRP) Ordinance will further support the improvement of both public and active transport systems in the city. These efforts are all aligned under the upcoming 10-Year Transport Master Plan, which will serve as the umbrella framework to guide Butuan toward a more sustainable, inclusive, and climate-adaptive transportation system.

Hue City's jurisdiction acknowledges that passenger mode share data is currently unavailable. To address this gap, the city will implement a structured data collection program between 2026 and 2027, led by the Department of Construction in collaboration with international partners (e.g., GIZ, UNDP, WWF, etc.). Planned activities include: 
Origin-Destination (O/D) Surveys: Household and roadside surveys to capture travel patterns, trip purposes, and preferred transport modes across urban and peri-urban areas. 
Traffic Counts: Manual and automated counts at key intersections and corridors to measure flows of motorcycles, cars, buses, bicycles, and pedestrians. 
Public Transport Data: Integration of ticketing and ridership statistics from the existing bus system and new e-bike/bicycle sharing schemes (e.g., GCOO, Vietsoftpro). 
GPS and Mobile Data: Collaboration with telecom operators and app-based mobility providers to access anonymized travel data for cross-validation. 
Cycling & Walking Audits: Periodic monitoring of dedicated pedestrian and cycling routes to assess modal shifts from private vehicles to active transport. 
Outputs and timeline: Baseline passenger mode share dataset available by the end of 2027. Updated every 3-5 years, aligned with Hue's Climate Action Plan monitoring cycle. Results to be published in the city's annual climate and transport report, and used for GHG inventory updates under the CIRIS system.

The transport system of the City of Balanga is defined by a strong reliance on public and informal transport modes, complemented by private vehicles and a modest share of active transport.

A majority of daily trips are served by informal and paratransit systems, including tricycles, jeepneys, and UV Express vans. These modes account for approximately 65-70% of all passenger trips, making them the backbone of mobility in both urban and barangay-level travel. Tricycles dominate short-distance commutes within barangays, while jeepneys and UV Express vans provide medium-distance connections to neighboring municipalities and Metro Manila.

Private motorized transport represents about 15-20% of trips, composed largely of motorcycles and, to a lesser extent, private cars. Motorcycle ownership is expanding more rapidly than cars due to affordability, making it an increasingly important contributor to urban mobility. While private vehicles offer convenience, their growth adds to congestion and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

Active transport still plays a notable role. Walking accounts for around 12% of total trips, particularly in central business districts and densely populated barangays where essential services are within short distances. Cycling remains limited at 1-2%, largely due to the lack of dedicated infrastructure and safety concerns, although there was a modest increase in use during the COVID-19 pandemic. Micromobility, including e-scooters and e-bikes, is emerging but still minimal, contributing less than 1% of trips.

Rail, metro, or tram systems are not yet present in Balanga, giving them a 0% share. Similarly, despite the city's coastal location along Manila Bay, ferry or river boat transport is not part of regular passenger mobility, leaving this category at 0% as well.

Finally, “other” modes of transport, such as company shuttles, school buses, and private vans, contribute a very small share, estimated at 1% or less of total trips.

Pode dar uma A estimativa da distribuição dos meios de transporte reflete a realidade urbana e rural do município:

Transporte individual motorizado (carros e motos - 50%): predominante devido à estrutura viária voltada ao transporte rodoviário e à necessidade de deslocamentos médios e longos entre a área urbana e a extensa zona rural.

Transporte coletivo (ônibus - 15%): utilizado principalmente por estudantes, trabalhadores e moradores de bairros periféricos. A cobertura é limitada, o que reduz sua participação no total de deslocamentos.

A pé (20%): significativo nos trajetos curtos no centro da cidade e em bairros próximos, compatível com o porte médio/pequeno do município.

Bicicleta (10%): meio de transporte tradicional, favorecido pela topografia relativamente plana em parte da área urbana, com uso frequente por estudantes e trabalhadores.

Elétricos leves (0-1%): ainda incipiente no município, com uso restrito de bicicletas elétricas ou patinetes, sem impacto estatístico relevante.

Outros (5%): inclui transporte por táxis, aplicativos e veículos fretados (escolares e coletivos específicos).

Essa distribuição evidencia a forte dependência do transporte individual, mas também mostra a relevância da mobilidade ativa (a pé e bicicleta), típica de municípios de porte semelhante.

Además, San Borja tiene una temperatura promedio baja durante todo el año, lo que beneficia la eficiencia de las células solares. Por lo tanto, este estudio recomienda que se evalúen fuentes de energía solar a pequeña escala.
